redaction_policy: Capture shapes, dtypes, counts, versions, and redacted paths. Never capture raw secrets or private dataset values by default.

cards.title: Operands cannot broadcast

triggers.pattern: operands could not be broadcast together|shape mismatch

cards.plain_cause: The two shapes cannot be aligned under NumPy's trailing-axis broadcasting rules.
likely_causes: Feature and batch axes were swapped.
A required length-one axis is missing.
Two genuinely different feature counts were combined.
checks: Right-align both shapes.
For each pair, require equality or a 1.
Name the semantic role of every axis before reshaping.
safe_fixes: Correct the upstream shape contract.
Use expand_dims or reshape only when the missing axis is semantically real.
Add a unit test for the intended shape pair.
never_actions: Do not flatten inputs just to silence the error.
Do not tile large arrays when broadcasting is sufficient.

cards.title: Matrix multiplication dimensions disagree

triggers.pattern: matmul: Input operand|core dimension|size [0-9]+ is different

cards.plain_cause: The left operand's last dimension does not equal the right operand's second-to-last dimension.
likely_causes: A weight matrix was transposed incorrectly.
Samples are arranged as columns in one place and rows in another.
The configured input feature count is wrong.
checks: Label the operation as (..., m, k) @ (..., k, n).
Compare the two k dimensions.
Verify the preceding layer's documented output shape.
safe_fixes: Correct the layer configuration or the one incorrect transpose.
Add forward shape assertions at the layer boundary.
never_actions: Do not transpose repeatedly until the exception disappears; verify semantics first.

cards.title: NaN or infinity appeared

triggers.pattern: invalid value encountered|overflow encountered|divide by zero

cards.plain_cause: A numerical operation produced a value outside the usable finite range or an undefined result.
likely_causes: Exponentials or products overflowed.
A logarithm, square root, or division received an invalid input.
A high learning rate caused parameter or gradient explosion.
The input already contained non-finite values.
checks: Find the first non-finite operation, not only the final loss.
Check inputs and gradients with isfinite.
Inspect domain assumptions and value scale.
safe_fixes: Use stable formulations and explicit domain validation.
Normalize inputs or lower the learning rate after confirming gradients are correct.
Add a regression fixture containing the failing scale.
never_actions: Do not replace NaN with zero without locating its origin.
Do not hide warnings globally.

cards.title: Softmax overflow or invalid probabilities
cards.plain_cause: Exponentiating raw logits overflowed, underflowed, or normalized along the wrong axis.
likely_causes: The maximum logit was not subtracted.
The reduction axis is not the class axis.
Probabilities were passed into a loss that expects logits.
checks: Subtract max(logits) with keepdims along the class axis.
Verify every probability row is finite, nonnegative, and sums to one.
Confirm the loss input contract.
safe_fixes: Implement shifted softmax or a combined stable log-softmax/cross-entropy.
Test logits [-1000, 0, 1000] and batched multidimensional cases.
never_actions: Do not clip probabilities until the unstable operation is understood.

cards.title: Gradient contributions were lost or left stale
cards.plain_cause: A tensor used along multiple graph paths had one contribution overwrite another, or a previous step's gradient was unintentionally reused.
likely_causes: Backward assigned instead of added at a branch join.
zero_grad was omitted between independent optimizer steps.
Repeated backward semantics were not defined.
checks: Compare a branched expression such as x*x + x.
Check whether every incoming edge contributes exactly once.
Separate intentional micro-batch accumulation from stale state.
safe_fixes: Add contributions at graph joins.
Clear parameter gradients at the documented training-loop point.
Add branch and repeated-backward tests.
never_actions: Do not always overwrite or always preserve gradients; make lifecycle semantics explicit.

cards.title: Broadcasted gradient did not return to input shape
cards.plain_cause: The backward rule kept repeated output axes instead of summing them back to the original input shape.
likely_causes: A bias gradient retained the batch axis.
Leading axes introduced during broadcasting were not reduced.
Original length-one axes were reduced without keepdims.
checks: Remove extra leading axes by summation.
Sum every original axis of length one with keepdims.
Assert the final gradient shape exactly equals the input shape.
safe_fixes: Centralize a tested sum-to-shape helper.
Gradient-check scalar, bias, and multi-axis broadcast cases.
never_actions: Do not reshape away extra values without summing their contributions.

cards.title: Training loss is rising, oscillating, or exploding
cards.plain_cause: Optimizer updates are not moving the current model toward a stable lower objective.
likely_causes: Learning rate is too high.
A derivative sign, scale, or batch reduction is wrong.
Inputs are badly scaled.
Initialization or activation choice causes unstable gradients.
The target/loss pairing is incorrect.
checks: Pass finite-difference checks before tuning.
Overfit one small fixed batch.
Compare update direction and magnitude for one parameter.
Inspect input, activation, and gradient scales layer by layer.
safe_fixes: Correct math or reduction errors first.
Then lower learning rate, normalize inputs, or use variance-aware initialization one change at a time.
Preserve the failing run configuration for comparison.
never_actions: Do not tune many hyperparameters simultaneously.
Do not treat a lower training loss as proof of leak-free evaluation.

cards.title: Path leaves the private workspace boundary

triggers.pattern: Path escapes the private workspace|outside the private projects directory|workspace must be outside

cards.plain_cause: The requested file resolves outside the configured private workspace or places the private workspace inside the public source tree.
likely_causes: A relative path contains parent traversal.
A symlink or junction resolves elsewhere.
The source or workspace root was configured incorrectly.
checks: Resolve both path and allowed root before comparison.
Check symlinks/junctions and drive changes.
Confirm user projects and source use separate roots.
safe_fixes: Choose a location beneath the private workspace.
Move the workspace outside the source repository.
Require explicit user confirmation for any root change.
never_actions: Do not disable the boundary check for convenience.
Do not log private full paths in public reports.

cards.title: An ignored path is still tracked
cards.plain_cause: .gitignore filters untracked paths; it does not remove a file already stored in the index or history.
likely_causes: The file was staged before the ignore rule existed.
A broad add operation captured private output.
The ignore pattern matches a different relative path than expected.
checks: Run git check-ignore -v for the path.
Run git ls-files for tracked state.
Inspect the outgoing commit range for earlier copies.
safe_fixes: Stop tracking the file without deleting the private working copy, then commit that removal.
Rotate any exposed credential and assess history cleanup separately.
Keep user workspaces outside the repository.
never_actions: Do not assume adding an ignore rule removes history.
Do not run destructive history rewriting automatically.

cards.title: Push rejected because the remote moved

triggers.pattern: non-fast-forward|fetch first|failed to push some refs

cards.plain_cause: The remote branch contains commits that are not in the local branch, so Git refused to discard them.
likely_causes: Another contributor pushed first.
The same branch changed on another machine.
Local history was rewritten.
checks: Fetch without merging.
Review the local-versus-remote log and diff.
Choose merge or rebase according to repository policy.
safe_fixes: Integrate reviewed remote work, resolve conflicts, rerun tests and the push guard, then push.
Ask a maintainer before any force operation.
never_actions: Do not default to force push.
Do not pull and execute unreviewed changes inside a privileged environment.

cards.title: A credential or secret may be in the outgoing content
cards.plain_cause: A token, private key, password, or similar credential pattern was found before publication.
likely_causes: A local configuration file was staged.
A token was pasted into code, a notebook, test fixture, log, or screenshot.
A generated credential file was not excluded.
checks: Do not display the value.
Determine whether it is real and whether it reached any remote or shared backup.
Inspect history, logs, artifacts, and forks within the exposure scope.
safe_fixes: Stop the push and remove the value from staged content.
Rotate or revoke a real credential immediately.
Use environment-based secret storage and add defense-in-depth ignore rules.
never_actions: Do not bypass because the repository is private.
Do not paste the secret into an issue or report.
Do not treat deletion alone as revocation.

cards.title: A dependency advisory has no known patched version
cards.plain_cause: The advisory applies to a dependency, but the advisory data does not identify a release that removes the vulnerability.
likely_causes: The maintainer has not released a fix.
The package is abandoned.
The vulnerable component is transitive or optional.
Advisory metadata is incomplete or newly published.
checks: Verify the exact dependency path and affected range.
Assess whether the vulnerable feature is included and reachable.
Look for an official fixed release, maintained replacement, or upstream mitigation.
safe_fixes: Remove, replace, isolate, or disable the affected component.
Document a time-bounded risk acceptance with owner and evidence only when policy permits.
Keep the push blocked when the release policy threshold is exceeded.
never_actions: Do not claim an automatic fix exists.
Do not dismiss an alert solely to make the gate green.
Do not silently upgrade to an untested fork.

cards.title: Untrusted pickle checkpoint refused
cards.plain_cause: Pickle reconstructs Python objects and can execute attacker-controlled code while loading.
likely_causes: A model checkpoint came from an unknown source.
An older tutorial serialized an entire model object.
A file extension was renamed without changing its format.
checks: Do not import or inspect the object by unpickling it.
Confirm provenance and format using non-executing metadata where possible.
Ask the trusted producer to export named numeric arrays and validated JSON metadata.
safe_fixes: Use Daedalus NPZ plus JSON checkpoints with allow_pickle disabled.
Validate checksum, schema, keys, shapes, and dtypes before loading arrays.
never_actions: Do not load the file to see what it contains.
Do not rely on antivirus or a renamed extension as a safety boundary.
